title: Random Forest
interviewAnswer: Random forests reduce tree variance by training many trees on bootstrapped samples and random feature subsets, then averaging or voting their predictions.
why: Random forests are robust tabular baselines and illustrate how bagging reduces variance.
intuition: Train many decision trees on different bootstrap samples and random feature subsets, then average/vote. Individual trees are unstable; averaging makes the ensemble more stable.
deepDive: Bootstrap sampling decorrelates training data, and random feature selection decorrelates trees further. Averaging reduces variance when errors are not perfectly correlated. Out-of-bag samples can estimate performance. Forests capture nonlinear interactions with modest preprocessing but can be large/slow and less interpretable than a single tree.
math: Regression forest: ŷ(x)=1/T Σ_t h_t(x); classification averages probabilities/votes.
workedExample: On mixed tabular sensor/product data, a forest can establish a strong nonlinear baseline before investing in neural networks.
commonMistakes: Saying bagging and boosting are the same.
Assuming more trees overfit like a single deeper tree; usually variance stabilizes though cost rises.
production: Forests are simple to serve but model size can be large. Validate preprocessing/category handling and benchmark latency/memory against boosting/linear alternatives.

lab.goal: Train and validate a Random Forest classifier.
lab.buildIt:
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
X,y=make_classification(n_samples=800,n_features=12,n_informative=5,random_state=0)
Xtr,Xte,ytr,yte=train_test_split(X,y,test_size=.25,random_state=0,stratify=y)
lab.useIt:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
m=RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200,min_samples_leaf=3,random_state=0,n_jobs=-1).fit(Xtr,ytr)
p=m.predict_proba(Xte)[:,1]
auc=roc_auc_score(yte,p)
print(auc)
lab.shipIt: Version features and forest hyperparameters; monitor score calibration and feature/data drift rather than relying only on training feature importance.
